text_blocks.snippet: "Cancer pulmon" is the Spanish term for lung cancer. It refers to a malignant tumor that originates in the tissues of the lungs. Lung cancer is primarily caused by genetic damage to DNA, often due to cigarette smoking or exposure to harmful chemicals.
snippet_highlighted_words: the Spanish term for lung cancer

list.title: Types:
list.snippet: Lung cancer is broadly classified into two main types: non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) (more common) and small cell lung cancer (SCLC).

list.title: Risk Factors:
list.snippet: Smoking is the leading risk factor, but other factors include exposure to secondhand smoke, asbestos, radon, certain air pollutants, and a family history of lung cancer.

list.title: Symptoms:
list.snippet: Early symptoms can be subtle, such as a persistent cough, coughing up blood, chest pain, shortness of breath, and fatigue.

list.title: Diagnosis:
list.snippet: Diagnosis involves various tests, including imaging scans (like CT scans), biopsies (to examine lung tissue samples), and sputum analysis.
